title: Four European Allies Sign $2.2B Deal for Polish Piorun MANPADS as UK Moves to Enable SCALP Assembly in Ukraine
subhead: Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia signed a framework agreement worth over 8 billion zloty ($2.2 billion) for Polish Piorun man-portable air-defense systems, while UK PM Andy Burnham's first overseas trip will release MBDA classified data to help France and Ukraine set up local SCALP cruise missile assembly lines.

sections.heading: Four-Nation European Deal for Polish Piorun MANPADS
sections.body: Poland, Norway, Lithuania and Latvia signed a framework agreement to buy Piorun (Thunderbolt) man-portable air-defense systems from Polish state group PGZ in a deal worth more than 8 billion zloty ($2.2 billion), Defense News reports. The acquisition covers 'several thousand missiles and several hundred launch units,' with deliveries to be completed by 2030 and Poland leading the consortium. More than 80% of the gear goes to the Polish military, financed partly through the EU's Security Action For Europe (SAFE) scheme, which foresees around €43.7 billion ($50.9 billion) in low-cost loans for Warsaw. Deputy Defence Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka said it is the first time the Armament Agency is buying not only for Polish forces but also for allied militaries. PGZ has scaled Piorun missile production from 300 to 1,500 units annually, targeting more than 2,000, and has sold the system to the US, Japan and Indonesia. A new Piorun New Generation (NG) variant with longer range is in development.
sections.whyItMatters: This is a concrete test of the EU's SAFE loan mechanism and of Poland's ambition to become a European defense industrial hub — four NATO allies pooling demand behind a single proven-in-Ukraine system rather than buying separately.

sections.heading: UK to Release SCALP Tech Data for Ukraine Assembly Lines
sections.body: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will make his first overseas trip since taking office to Ukraine on Monday, co-chairing a Coalition of the Willing meeting and meeting President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Reuters reports. He is set to announce that Britain has agreed to let European missile maker MBDA release classified information on British-made components used in the SCALP long-range cruise missile, enabling France and Ukraine to establish local assembly lines for the missile, which shares British and French technology. 'Ukraine's security is our security,' Burnham said. Britain has pledged more than £25 billion ($34 billion) in military and civilian support since 2022. Moscow warned London last week of 'consequences' for supplying drones to Kyiv after reports that British-made drones were used in long-range strikes on Russia for the first time.
sections.whyItMatters: This follows last week's authorization of SCALP/Storm Shadow assembly in Ukraine and deepens the shift from donating finished weapons to co-producing them inside Ukraine — a model that changes how Western defense firms and Kyiv's industrial base interact.

sections.heading: US Navy's Silent Anvil: A Glide Torpedo for Anti-Submarine Warfare
sections.body: The US Navy is exploring two options for its Silent Anvil Air-Launched Torpedo (SAA-LT) and has issued a Request for Information, Defense News reports. The first is a new torpedo launched from an aircraft or drone that glides into the water and acoustically homes on its target; the second is a glide kit affixed to an existing torpedo. The concept extends the Navy's existing High Altitude Anti-Submarine Warfare Weapon Capability, which added a glide kit to Mark 54 torpedoes launched from P-8 Poseidon patrol planes. The Navy wants a compact weapon similar in form factor to the GBU-39 Small Diameter Bomb — no more than 268 pounds, 70 inches long, 7.5 inches in diameter — compatible with a standard BRU-61/A bomb rack and launchable from manned and unmanned platforms up to 60,000 feet. The RFI deadline is Sept. 29, with a prototype due within 18 months of award and 180 all-up-round prototypes within three years. The program comes as China expands the size and sophistication of its submarine fleet, including large long-range robot subs.
sections.whyItMatters: Silent Anvil signals the Navy is pushing anti-submarine weapons onto unmanned, high-altitude platforms — a response to China's growing submarine force and a bet that cheap glide kits can extend the reach of existing torpedoes.

sections.heading: Italy Eyes US APKWS Kits to Turn Cheap Missiles Into Drone Killers
sections.body: The Italian Air Force is mulling the purchase of US technology that converts cheap unguided missiles into precision weapons for counter-drone work, Defense News reports. The potential deal follows US State Department approval of a Foreign Military Sale to Italy of 5,031 BAE Systems Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS) II guidance systems, worth up to $364 million including launchers, warheads, rocket motors and support. The APKWS inserts between a missile's warhead and motor, adding four fold-out wings with laser seekers to turn a missile costing under €100,000 ($117,000) into a guided weapon — versus an AMRAAM that costs roughly ten times more. The likely recipient is Italy's Eurofighter, which is already guarding Europe's borders against drone incursions; an Italian Eurofighter on a NATO Baltic air-policing mission shot down an unidentified drone in Latvian airspace this month. The RAF already uses APKWS on its Eurofighters after a two-month rapid acquisition.
sections.whyItMatters: The economics of counter-drone warfare are driving a market for cheap precision guidance — turning legacy unguided rockets into low-cost interceptors rather than expending high-end air-to-air missiles on cheap drones.

sections.heading: Taiwan Discloses Strong Bow ABM Specs in Funding Push
sections.body: Taiwan's National Chung-Shan Institute of Science and Technology has disclosed key specifications of its locally developed Chiang Kung (Strong Bow) anti-ballistic missile system as the government seeks legislative funding for mass production, SCMP reports. The system, also called Tien Kung (Sky Bow) IV, is a land-based mid-tier anti-tactical ballistic missile interceptor designed to engage targets at altitudes of at least 70km (43 miles) — higher than Taiwan's existing Patriot and Tien Kung III systems. The vertically launched missile reaches hypersonic speeds with a two-stage solid-fuel motor, using inertial guidance and radar uplink corrections in midcourse before switching to an active seeker in the terminal phase. The defense ministry proposes spending NT$36.1 billion (US$1.13 billion) to produce two Strong Bow systems and 128 interceptor missiles, to be resubmitted through a supplementary budget after the system was excluded from a pared-back package approved by the opposition-controlled legislature in May.
sections.whyItMatters: Taiwan is pushing its own high-altitude interceptor as a complement to US-supplied Patriot systems, part of a broader effort to build indigenous missile defense as Beijing's pressure grows and the island pursues a record defense budget.

sections.heading: China Deploys J-16s to Egypt for Joint Drills; Expands Rocket Force Procurement Probe
sections.body: Chinese fighter jets conducted combat training with Egyptian counterparts after a major PLA Air Force deployment to the Middle East, SCMP reports. The PLA deployed J-16 fighters, YU-20 aerial tankers, KJ-500 airborne early warning aircraft and Z-20 helicopters, flying more than 6,000km (3,730 miles) over nine hours and crossing four countries to reach Egypt, with J-16s conducting aerial refueling from YU-20 tankers before landing on August 21. CCTV said the exercise tested long-range force projection, rapid deployment and integrated operations. Separately, China has called for public reports of suspected procurement corruption in the PLA Rocket Force (PLARF), inviting suppliers, bidding agencies, evaluation experts and military personnel to report violations across all stages of procurement, with reports accepted until November 30, 2026. The PLA made a similar public appeal in December 2025 regarding Air Force procurement irregularities.
sections.whyItMatters: The Egypt deployment demonstrates China's growing ability to project air power far beyond its borders and deepen defense ties in the Middle East, while the Rocket Force procurement probe signals continued anti-corruption pressure on the strategic missile branch.

bottomLine: Today's defense news centers on European industrial cooperation and the economics of modern warfare. Four NATO allies pooled demand behind Poland's Piorun MANPADS in a $2.2 billion deal financed partly through the EU's SAFE loan scheme, while the UK moved to enable SCALP cruise missile assembly inside Ukraine — both signs that European defense is consolidating production and shifting toward co-production with Kyiv. The US Navy's Silent Anvil glide torpedo and Italy's APKWS drone-interceptor purchase reflect a broader push for cheaper, platform-agnostic weapons. In Asia, Taiwan disclosed specs for its indigenous Strong Bow interceptor in a funding push, and China demonstrated long-range air power projection with a J-16 deployment to Egypt while expanding its Rocket Force procurement probe.
